- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to under-forecast; adjust upward by 1–2% of recent mean.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤-0.5), model tends to over-forecast; adjust downward by 1–2% of recent mean.
- After a sharp price spike (≥5% from prior peak), model often overshoots; reduce forecast by 3–5% in next 3–5 days.
- Model frequently underestimates mean-reversion periods; if sentiment is neutral or mixed, add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to capture rebound.
- For 30-day horizon, model often lags by 1–3 days; if sentiment is trending, shift forecast 1–2 days ahead with slight upward bias.
- If sentiment flips from negative to positive within 5 days, model often misses the reversal; adjust forecast to match sentiment shift within 2–3 days.
